name: Cheek poke
blurb: A fingertip pressed into the cheek: a soft, cute pose with a hint of thinking or teasing
title: Cheek Poke Pose: Finger to Cheek Drawing & Photo Reference
description: Cheek poke pose reference: the finger to cheek gesture, from cute self-poke to poking a friend's puffed cheek, with drawing tips and soft-light photo advice.
answer: The cheek poke is a pose where a fingertip, usually the index finger, presses lightly into the cheek. On your own face it looks cute or thoughtful; poking someone else's cheek, often a puffed one, is a playful, affectionate tease.

sections.h: What a finger to cheek says
body: Touching the face draws attention to it, and pressing a fingertip into the soft cheek emphasises roundness and youthfulness. A self-poke with a smile says cute; with eyes looking up and to the side it says pondering. Poking someone else turns it into an interaction, the friendly tease of siblings, close friends or a couple.
There is also the old prank: tap a friend on the far shoulder and leave a finger out, so their cheek lands on it when they turn.

ul: Single finger, smiling: index fingertip just below the cheekbone, head tilted toward it.
Double poke: both index fingers in both cheeks, a wide closed-eye smile.
Thinking poke: finger on the cheek, eyes up and to the side, lips slightly pursed.
Puffed-cheek poke: cheeks full of air, finger about to let it out.
Poking a friend: one person pokes, the other reacts with a pout or a laugh.
Prank poke: finger waiting where a turning cheek will meet it.

sections.h: How to draw a cheek poke
body: Place the fingertip where the cheek is fullest, a little below and in front of the cheekbone. The cheek should dent slightly: pull the face outline inward around the fingertip and add a small curved shadow line beside it. Without that dent the finger looks like it is floating in front of the face.

Bend the poking finger slightly at the last joint and fold the others loosely; the thumb can rest against the side of the middle finger. Lift the mouth corner on the poked side a little, because pressure pushes it up. A touch of blush around the fingertip helps in anime styles.
Press gently. A hard poke distorts the face and looks uncomfortable; a light touch with the finger angled from below reads as cute. Turn the face slightly toward the poking hand so both are in focus.
Soft, frontal light shows the small dent and the cheek's roundness without harsh shadows. For two-person poke shots, shoot a short burst; the reaction a beat later is usually the best frame.

faq.q: What does poking your own cheek mean in photos?
faq.a: It is a cute, playful pose, sometimes with a thinking look. It draws attention to the face and its roundness.

faq.q: How do I draw a finger pressing into a cheek?
faq.a: Dent the cheek outline around the fingertip, add a small shadow beside the dent and lift the mouth corner on that side.

faq.q: What is the shoulder tap cheek poke prank?
faq.a: Tapping someone's far shoulder with a finger left extended, so their cheek lands on it when they turn around.
